details.recommendedFor: Users who want less telemetry and background data collection while keeping core Windows features.
benefits: Reduces non-essential data collection and chatter.
Can lower background CPU, disk, and network activity.
tradeoffs: Some personalization and Microsoft recommendations may be reduced.
Troubleshooting data available to support tools can be limited.
riskNotes: Review enterprise or school compliance requirements before disabling diagnostics.
Avoid disabling settings required by anti-cheat or managed environments.
details.reversible: Usually reversible by restoring privacy defaults or using the tweak revert action.

details.recommendedFor: Competitive players and latency-focused users who prioritize responsiveness over idle efficiency.
benefits: Improves scheduling consistency for foreground workloads.
Can reduce frame-time spikes in CPU-bound scenarios.
tradeoffs: Higher power draw and potentially more heat/noise.
Battery runtime and idle efficiency may decrease.
riskNotes: Aggressive scheduling can impact workstation/background tasks.
Validate thermal headroom before long gaming sessions.
details.reversible: Revert by restoring Balanced/default power and scheduler values.

details.recommendedFor: GPU-bound or high-refresh players tuning render latency.
benefits: Can lower input-to-photon latency in supported games.
May stabilize frame delivery by tightening queue behavior.
tradeoffs: Aggressive queue limits can reduce peak FPS in some titles.
Driver-level overrides may conflict with in-game settings.
riskNotes: Test per game engine; ideal settings vary by DX11/DX12/Vulkan.
Keep a known-good driver profile for quick rollback.
details.reversible: Yes, by restoring driver defaults or applying tweak revert.

details.recommendedFor: Online gamers optimizing packet priority and latency consistency.
benefits: Can reduce jitter and improve packet scheduling under load.
Improves per-game traffic prioritization with QoS/DSCP policies.
tradeoffs: Benefit depends on router/ISP honoring QoS tags.
Incorrect adapter values can reduce throughput or compatibility.
riskNotes: Document original NIC values before applying advanced changes.
Enterprise/VPN environments may override local QoS behavior.
details.reversible: Yes, remove policies and restore adapter defaults.

details.recommendedFor: Advanced users balancing low overhead with acceptable baseline security.
benefits: Can reduce scanning overhead on trusted gaming workloads.
Allows tighter control of security modules during sessions.
tradeoffs: Could increase exposure when downloading untrusted files.
riskNotes: Use only on trusted systems with strong browsing hygiene.
Re-enable protections after testing or competitive sessions.

details.recommendedFor: Users trimming persistent background load for lower latency.
benefits: Frees RAM/CPU resources from non-essential services.
Reduces startup contention and background wakeups.
tradeoffs: Certain Windows or vendor features may stop working.
OS updates may re-enable disabled services/tasks.
riskNotes: Disable only services you can identify and restore.
Keep restore points for aggressive service profiles.
details.reversible: Partially reversible if startup modes are preserved in revert steps.

details.recommendedFor: Clean installations or power users removing bundled software.
benefits: Reduces clutter and background app activity.
tradeoffs: Removed apps may need manual reinstallation later.
Some OEM convenience features can be lost.
riskNotes: Confirm dependencies before removing Microsoft Store components.
Prefer staged cleanup over one-shot aggressive removal.
details.reversible: Some removals are reversible, but certain packages may require manual reinstall.

details.recommendedFor: Players who want per-game DSCP 46 policy automation.
benefits: Simplifies policy cleanup with matching revert actions.
